blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 78 in June to 67 in October (−14.1%), and it took 11.8% of the city’s 357 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 193 in June to 185 in October (−4.1%), and it took 20.5% of the city’s 694 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Langley City for detached houses in July, October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, August (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Board geography: the Langley City sub-area is one of 11 sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Langley" (Aldergrove, Brookswood, Campbell Valley, County Line Glen Valley, Fort Langley, Langley City, Murrayville, Otter District, Salmon River, Walnut Grove, Willoughby Heights).

Where the condo stock concentrates: the City's verified apartment stock is a single older cluster — three 1988–1990 buildings within a few blocks of each other around 205 Street, 206 Street and 53 Avenue in the downtown core.

Langley City sub-area, September 2026 — the area's own figures (inventory / solds / sales ratio): Detached 64 / 8 / 13%; Condos & Townhomes 195 / 34 / 17% (joint with Aldergrove in the Langley set, below Murrayville 23%, Willoughby Heights 19% and Walnut Grove 18%). SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, and the only community here is the combined City + Township "Langley" — so there is no published median for the City of Langley alone: per-sub-area medians are not verified.

items.t: Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 3300): a secondary suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the gross floor area of the building; the registered owner must reside on the lot; at least one extra off-street parking space is required; and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry.

Langley City property taxes: payments received after the July 2 due date incur a penalty; the City's payment page lists City Hall at 20399 Douglas Crescent and a 2.2% processing fee on credit-card payments. blocks.text: Good to know about Langley City

items.t: Parkway Estates (1988), Parkway II (1989) and Glenmont Park (1990) stand within a few blocks of each other around 205 Street, 206 Street and 53 Avenue, and all three are published as 55+ communities — a City condo search is, in practice, a search of those three buildings and their strata documents, whatever the 252-result feed suggests.
Its build year is itself unsettled — 1991 per listings, 1990 per the building directory.

Two addresses ten numbers apart are different buildings with different records. Glenmont Park is 5375 205 St (verified); Morningside Estates is 5365 205 St (Not confirmed). Directory and listing searches blur the pair — verify the civic address on the Form B before importing any fact from one to the other.

The Langleys' hospital is not in the City. Langley Memorial Hospital's Fraser Health listing places it at 22051 Fraser Highway, in the Township of Langley, immediately outside the City boundary, though it is the hospital City residents use.
The City's zoning bylaw is new, and its adoption date is genuinely unsettled in sources.

Langley City has no station today; the City's own vision page states SkyTrain is coming "by the end of 2029" — pricing a City condo on a station that does not yet exist is pricing the City's published anticipation, not current service.
The City shelf and the Township shelf move differently.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Langley City

items.t: Zoning — City: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300 governs the City; it repeals Zoning Bylaw 1996 No. 2100. Minimum lot sizes (Bylaw 3300, as printed): R1 Suburban Residential — 557 m² / 16 m frontage; R2 Townhouse Residential — 1,000 m², except lots created by subdivision with a registered party wall agreement (maximum 280 m², minimum frontage 4.5 m); R3 Low Rise Residential — 1,000 m² / 26.0 m. Township Bylaw 2500 does not apply here.

SSMUH — City: the City amended its Zoning Bylaw to permit small-scale multi-unit housing on RS1 and RS2 lots by Bylaw No. This is the CITY's own SSMUH frame; the Township's Bylaw 6020 frame is different and is never imported here.

Suites — City: a City secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the principal dwelling's gross floor area; the registered owner must reside on the lot; at least one extra off-street parking space is required; and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry.

Subdivision — City: Bylaw 3300 states "No person shall subdivide land except in accordance with this bylaw"; subdivisions are subject to the City's Subdivision Control Bylaw and Development Cost Charge Bylaw; a lot created by subdivision must meet its zone's minimum lot area; and meeting the minimum standards does not bind the Approving Officer to approve. City DCC Bylaw 2024 No. 3256.

Strata block (bare-land strata parcels, if met): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Langley City
Local rules that affect duplexes in Langley City

items.t: SSMUH and suites (Langley City): The City amended its Zoning Bylaw to permit small-scale multi-unit housing on RS1 and RS2 lots by Bylaw No. 3284, adopted June 17, 2024 — RS1/RS2 permit 4 units, and 6 units if within 400 m of a frequent bus stop (the City's own tier — the Township has no 6-unit tier, and the two are never blended). Secondary suites (Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300): A suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the gross floor area of the building — the City's own cap, never borrowed — the registered owner must reside on the lot, at least one extra off-street parking space is required, and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry. That cap applies to a suite inside a City duplex exactly as it applies to a suite in a single-family house.
